headline: High-risk git/workspace interaction: Aider can write and commit shared repo state while marker has no documented isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write git-tracked files and uses stdin/stdout, so a malicious document from marker could be copied into Aider’s context manually. Marker has no filesystem read/write or MCP surfaces, so there is no automatic bridge; the pathway is limited to unusual manual transfer.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes marker output into Aider prompts or files
IF marker content is treated as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep marker outputs in a separate review pane
Paste only extracted text, not raw instructions
Add a short prompt prefix stating marker output is untrusted
Use a checklist to strip executable-looking text before handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress broadly, while marker has no filesystem access or network egress. The pair does not show an automatic shared data channel, so leakage is mainly via operator-mediated transfer of repo contents into marker or vice versa.
conditions: IF the operator feeds repository files into marker for processing
IF marker outputs are copied back into Aider without redaction
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the repo before running either tool
Redact credentials before sending text to marker
Use a throwaway branch for any sensitive files
Review marker inputs for PHI, keys, and tokens

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. Marker has no write capability, so direct write-write conflict is absent, but Aider instances can still collide on the same repo state in default use.
conditions: IF two Aider sessions operate on the same git repository
IF marker-generated edits are applied into the same working tree
mitigations: Use one writer per repo at a time
Create separate branches for parallel work
Run git status before each commit
Resolve conflicts immediately after each marker-driven edit

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate and commit code changes, and marker is a document-processing agent with no verification surface shown. If marker output is treated as authoritative input to Aider, errors can cascade into committed repo changes; the pair lacks a documented verification step.
conditions: IF marker output is used as the sole source for Aider edits
IF Aider commits changes without human review
mitigations: Require human review before commit
Cross-check marker outputs against source documents
Ask Aider to cite the exact source lines it used
Reject edits that lack traceable provenance

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and provider API keys, while marker’s profile lists no data classes or residency controls. The main compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen sensitive content flowing into Aider’s third-party model providers; marker is not cited because no residency or retention obligations are documented for it.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are sent through Aider to external model providers
IF marker is used on regulated documents and its outputs are stored in the same repo
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared repo
Use a local-only model configuration where possible
Strip secrets before invoking Aider
Document retention rules for any marker outputs
